note_sections:
- Title: Free underexpanded jets in a quiescent medium: A review
- Paper ID / source record: B004 / B-T-04
- Original PDF: `02_PDF_Raw/B/B-T-04_2015_Franquet_FreeUnderexpanded_Jets_Review.pdf`
Review-level underexpanded-jet framework and confidence audit.
Which geometric, shock-structure, and similarity relations for axisymmetric free underexpanded jets are reliable, and where does the literature remain quantitatively uncertain?
Review centered on experimental literature, with theoretical/numerical context and thermodynamic-model discussion.
Axisymmetric free jets into quiescent media; convergent and convergent-divergent nozzles are distinguished.
Pressure definitions are explicit: eta_0=P_0/P_infinity and eta_e=P_e/P_infinity; they are not interchangeable.
Near field contains core and mixing layer; regular reflection yields diamond cells, singular reflection yields a Mach disk/barrel shock, and extreme underexpansion can become first-cell dominated.
NA: no liquid droplet or spray case is investigated.
Pressure-ratio and Mach-number definitions are treated contextually; correlations depend on total versus exit pressure ratio, exit Mach number, gamma, and nozzle geometry.
Steady/quasi-steady spatial structure is reviewed; transient Mach-disk oscillation and hysteresis are noted but not normalized into one duration.
Mach-disk position collapses more consistently than diameter. Far-field profiles show self-similar hyperbolic decay when suitable equivalent-jet scaling is used.
The review retains L_MD/D_e=0.645497 sqrt(eta_0) for convergent nozzles and reports substantially larger uncertainty for diameter and other characteristic lengths.
Increasing pressure ratio is consistently associated with downstream Mach-disk displacement, while nozzle angle, gamma, and exit Mach effects on other quantities are not uniformly resolved.
Pressure-driven expansion -> shock/reflection pattern -> mixing-layer growth -> transition -> far-field self-similarity.
No reacting or ignition calculation; relevance is through gas-jet mixing and dilution physics.
Pressure-ratio definitions: PDF p.3; Mach-disk position: p.7; diameter: p.9; Mach-disk confidence summary: p.11; far-field conclusion: p.22; overall conclusion: p.24.
All numerical expressions are review-secondary correlations or reviewed ranges. They are not classified as primary experimental values.

Heterogeneous nozzle geometries, fluids, pressure definitions, and limited high-pressure data produce scatter. Curvature, cell disappearance, characteristic lengths, entrainment onset, and mixing-layer transition remain weakly constrained.

- T1-B004-C01: Mach-disk position is better constrained than other near-field quantities.
- T1-B004-C02: Far-field decay is robust but equivalent-nozzle normalization remains model-dependent.
Direct comparison with B009/B011/B028 requires matching pressure definition, nozzle geometry, and transient versus quasi-steady state.
None. Review limitations are representable with secondary-synthesis notes and NV; Schema 1.1 is unchanged.
Provides the canonical underexpanded-jet vocabulary and a map of robust versus unresolved scaling relations.

High-fidelity primary test of early internal-wave and pressure mechanisms across low/high gas-liquid wave-speed ratios.
Does reflected-expansion-wave focusing identify the NPP/cavitation site across liquid properties and shock strengths, and how must the theory change at high wave-speed ratio?
2D high-order compressible multiphase simulation with MFC plus improved ray-tracing model; cylindrical water/n-hexane droplets.
Planar incident shock, half-domain 14D0 x 6D0, 800 cells/D0, reflective symmetry boundary.
Pre-shock air and droplet start at atmospheric pressure. Ms spans 1.75-8.4; Table 1 preserves ppost/ppre, rhopost/rhopre, and n for both liquids.
Incident, transmitted, reflected, expansion waves and Mach stem form an internal wave envelope whose topology changes with n.
Water and n-hexane droplets; densities 1000 and 657 kg/m3 at NTP. No phase-transition model.
Ms is incident shock Mach in laboratory frame. We=rho_post u_post^2 D0/sigma and Re=rho_post u_post D0/mu; ranges and source-limited components are linked.
NPP history is figure-only; characteristic nondimensional occurrence is near t*=1.25, slightly earlier at higher Ms.
At low n the NPP and focus positions align; at high n the NPP tends toward a constant while theoretical focus shifts. Mach stem must be included.
Table 1 contains 12 Ms cases, pressure/density jump ratios, and liquid-specific n values; all are retained case-by-case.
Internal pressure evolution contains shock, relaxation, fluctuation, and expansion-wave contributions. Expansion focusing alone does not determine total NPP.
Incident/Mach-stem forcing -> transmitted/reflected wave envelope -> expansion contribution plus relaxation/fluctuation -> total NPP -> potential cavitation site.
No ignition/combustion; relevance is early pressure mechanism and possible cavitation/breakup consequences.
Configuration p.4; Table 1 and We/Re p.5; Table 2 p.6; NPP history p.9; NPP/focus trend p.13; improved model pp.20-22; factors pp.23-28; conclusion pp.28-29.

2D cylindrical geometry; no phase transition; cavitation location is inferred from NPP rather than directly resolved; model uses fitted Mach-stem trajectory.
